full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the case, are that the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.43 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Paikgachha, Khulna praying for declaration of title to 3.30 acres of land out of 7.57 acres land under B.S. Khatian No.71, S.A. Khatian No.114 of mouza Khatian contending, inter alia, that the land of C.S. Khatian No.771, mouza Khalia, measuring an area of 7.90 acres belonged to Shashadhar Bachhar and Bishnanpada Bachhar to the extent of 1/3 share who settled 2.31 acres of by patta dated 04.06.1963 in favour of the plaintiff. Thereafter, Bishnapada Bachhar sold 2.16 acres of land by a kabala deed dated 03.05.1945 in favour of the plaintiff. Out of those land 3.30 acres of land is the suit land. The plaintiff has been in possession in the suit land for more than 12 years. The share of Shashadhar Bachhar and others were sold in auction for arrears of rent and the said auction was purchased by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The plaintiff filed an application under Section 173 of the Bengal Tenancy Act for setting aside the auction thereupon Miscellaneous Case No.183 of 1960 was started. Ultimately, the said Miscellaneous case was ended compromise and the auction in respect of the suit land was set aside. Inspite of that the S.A. record was prepared in the name of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 wrongly. The Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 having no title and possession in the suit land denied the title of the plaintiff on the 5th of Chaitra, 1383 B.S. and as such, the suit. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit denying the plaintiffs case contending, inter alia, that the suit jote belonged to Kali Charan Bachar. For arrear rent, a rent suit being No.590 was started. The suit jote was sold in auction and that auction was purchased by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 14.03.1956. They got possession, through Court and paid rent and during their possession the S.A. Khatian recorded was correctly pre-pared in their names; that Shashadhar and others did not settle any land in favour of the plaintiff as claimed by them. On 04.06.1943 the plaintiffs were minor Shashadhar took a loan from Jharu Bachhar. As against the said loan a patta was executed and registered in favour of the plaintiff. That loan was paid within 1 year and the patta was returned back to Jharu Bachhar. The defendant has been in possession in the auction purchased land. The plaintiff No.2 was a judgment-debtor to the rent decree. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 ware not at all aware about the compromise made in Miscellaneous Case No.183 of 1960. If any document is found in support of said compromise that would be collusive, forged and not binding upon the defendant. They further stated that the plaintiff has filed a test suit. 

 5. It appears from the record that the total land comprised an area of 7.57 acres in C.S. Khatian No.71, S.A. Khatian No.114 of mouza Khalia out of which the plaintiff has sought for a declaration of title in respect of 3.30 acres of land without mentioning any boundary; that the plaintiff has failed to make out any case of amicable partition and also failed to make out a case of his exclusive possession; that the plaintiff has sought for declaration of title to 0.60 acre of land out of 0.90 acre of land from plot No.924 and also has sought for declaration of title to 0.013 acre of land out of 0.16 acre of land from plot No.946. This sort of declaration is barred under the proviso to Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.
